title: ARIMA / SARIMA
interviewAnswer: ARIMA combines autoregression, differencing and moving-average error terms. The p,d,q orders control lagged values, differencing and lagged forecast errors; SARIMA adds seasonal equivalents. I use it as a strong interpretable baseline when temporal dependence is meaningful.
why: ARIMA remains a valuable baseline: transparent, data-efficient and excellent for understanding whether complex models truly add value.
intuition: ARIMA predicts the present from a cleaned-up version of the past: first make the series sufficiently stable, then explain it with previous values and previous surprises.
deepDive: AR terms model dependence on lagged observations; MA terms model dependence on lagged innovations/residuals. Model selection should combine diagnostics, validation and domain knowledge, not just minimize AIC. Seasonal structure can be represented explicitly with SARIMA.
workedExample: If weekly demand depends strongly on the previous two weeks and residual shocks persist one step, ARIMA(2,1,1) might be a candidate after differencing a trend. Validate it against naive seasonal baselines.
commonMistakes: Thinking MA(q) means moving-average smoothing of observations.
Selecting p,d,q only from ACF/PACF and skipping backtesting.
followUps: What is the difference between AR and MA?
Why can a seasonal naive baseline beat ARIMA?
production: ARIMA is cheap to retrain and explain, making it a useful fallback/baseline even when a production stack later adopts boosted trees or neural forecasting.
math: ARIMA(p,d,q): apply d differences, then model with p autoregressive lags and q lagged innovations.

lab.goal: Fit an ARIMA baseline and inspect forecasts/residuals.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA
rng=np.random.default_rng(0); y=np.cumsum(rng.normal(size=120))
train,test=y[:100],y[100:]
fit=ARIMA(train,order=(1,1,1)).fit(); pred=fit.forecast(len(test))
print(pred[:3])
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error
naive=np.repeat(train[-1],len(test))
print('ARIMA MAE',mean_absolute_error(test,pred),'naive',mean_absolute_error(test,naive))
